name: Shao Xiaofeng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Shao Xiaofeng's fortune arises from his holdings in Ant Group, the financial services arm of China e-commerce leader Alibaba Group.
Shao has held positions in Alibaba-affiliated companies including chief risk officer at Alibaba Group itself and director at Alibaba Pictures.
China held up Ant's planned dual listing in Shanghai and Hong Kong on regulatory concerns on Nov. 3, 2020.

name: Jin Xin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2023); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026)
forbes_bio: Jin Xin chairs Dajin Heavy Industry, a supplier of offshore wind power equipment.

name: Shintaro Yamada
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2021-2022)
forbes_bio: Shintaro Yamada founded the online used-goods marketplace, Mercari, in 2013 and is the company's CEO.
Yamada launched the online marketplace focusing on smartphone users. It had achieved unicorn status by 2016.
Mercari's shares have more than doubled since 2020 on an online-buying boom during the pandemic.
The company gave each employee a grant of $550 to cover the cost of working from home during the coronavirus pandemic.
forbes_facts: Yamada is a big fan of retired Japanese pitcher Hideo Nomo, who played Nippon Professional Baseball and Major League Baseball.
In July 2019, Mercari bought a 62% stake in Japan's top-scoring soccer team, the Kashima Antlers, for $15 million.

name: Kanjibhai Virani
forbes_bio: Kanjibhai Virani is the cofounder of Indian snacks maker Balaji Wafers, which sells a range of items including packaged snacks, noodles and confectionery.

Virani and his two brothers Bhikhabhai and Chandubhai, who help him run the company, entered the three comma club after selling a minority stake to private equity giant General Atlantic in January 2026.
Before starting Balaji Wafers, the brothers were doing odd jobs at Astron Cinemas in the town of Rajkot in the western Indian state of Gujarat.
The name "Balaji" was inspired by a temple in their hometown.

name: Zhou Mingjie
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2015-2022); Hurun Global (2017-2022); Hurun China (2012-2022)
forbes_bio: Zhou Mingjie owns 70% of Ocean's King Lighting, a China lighting supplier.
Zhou worked at a construction materials company and a textile investment firm before he founded Ocean's King in 1995.

name: Yu Kai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun China (2019-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Yu Kai is the chairman and CEO of Beijing-based Horizon Robotics, which develops both the software and hardware needed for self-driving cars.
The company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in October 2024 in what was the bourse's largest IPO so far in the year, raising nearly $700 million.
Before it went public, Horizon has attracted investors including SAIC Motor, 5Y Capital, Hillhouse, HongShan and Volkswagen.
Horizon claims to be the largest Chinese provider of assisted and autonomous driving systems in the country by installation volume, counting Volkswagen, Hyundai Motor and BYD as its customers.
An AI scientist, Yu started an autonomous driving project at Baidu before cofounding Horizon Robotics in 2015 with other former Baidu employees.

name: Charles Beauduin
forbes_bio: Charles Beauduin controls the textile machinery company Vandewiele and 25% of listed company Barco, which specializes in high-end digital projection, imaging, and networking solutions.
The Beauduin family has its roots in the sugar industry and sold sugar factory Tiense Suiker to Germany's Südzucker in 1989.
In 1993 Beauduin took over Vandewiele group, which was founded in 1880 as a machinery servicing company and converted into a weaving machine manufacturer by Michel Van de Wiele in 1921.
The company produces textile machinery for flooring, home linen and fashion under brands that include Titan, Aros, Loepfe and Eutron.

name: Kim Hyun-tae
forbes_bio: Kim Hyun-tae is CEO of South Korean biotechnology company Voronoi.
Voronoi's two most promising cancer drug candidates are VRN10 and VRN11. Both started Phase 1 clinical trials in the first quarter of 2025.
Voronoi was founded by Kim's younger brother, Hyun-seok, in 2015. The older Kim took over the company in 2016 and listed it on Korea's Kosdaq in 2022.
Previously, Kim did stints as head of asset management at eBest Investment & Securities, Hanwha Investment & Securities and KB Securities.

name: Yi Feng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021-2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021); Hurun China (2010-2021)
forbes_bio: Feng Yi is vice general manager of of Sangfor Technologies, a supplier of IT infrastructure solutions.
Sangfor went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2018.
Feng worked for China telecommunications supplier ZTE after graduating from China University of Science and Technology in 1998.

name: Jerry Ng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2022)
forbes_bio: Veteran banker Jerry Ng, with more than three decades of experience, gets his wealth from a stake in Bank Jago.
He acquired shares of what was then called Bank Artos in December 2019.
Bank Jago is transforming itself into a digital bank and is looking to work with small and medium fintech enterprises.
Ng has previously held top positions at Bank Danamon Indonesia and Bank Central Asia. Until February 2019 Ng was president director of Bank BTPN.
Indonesia's payment and on-demand services app Gojek bought a stake in Bank Jago in 2020.
forbes_facts: He is a trustee at the Blum Center for Developing Economies at the University of California, Berkeley.
He was also the deputy chair of the Indonesian Bank Restructuring Agency.
